browser.label: Browser control
browser.title: Browser
browser.hint: Let the agent drive a real browser — navigate, click, fill forms, and read pages.
browser.description: Let the agent open pages, click, fill forms, and read the web — reusing your Chrome login.
browser.headedOffBody: You're reusing your Chrome login (“{{profile}}”), so the agent drives your real Chrome — it will usually still open a window even with this off, especially while Chrome is already running. For a true no-window (headless) browser, switch “Browse as” to the private browser.
browser.noChromeWillDownload: No Chrome detected — a private browser will be downloaded on first use.
browser.privateNote: Uses a separate downloaded browser that never touches your Chrome. Starts logged out; downloaded automatically on first use.
browser.reuseNote: Reuses a copy of “{{name}}”. The agent acts as that logged-in account; your real Chrome profile is never modified. Navigation still follows your approval mode.
browser.isolatedNote: Isolated profile — the agent starts logged out. Pick an account above to reuse its logins.
browser.downloaded: Browser downloaded — you can enable browser control now.
browser.capCore: Standard — navigate, click, read, screenshot, run JS
browser.allowedDomainsHint: One per line. Empty means no restriction. Supports patterns like *.example.com.

dataFlow.title: Privacy & data flow
dataFlow.subtitle: What stays on this machine, and exactly what leaves it.

local.heading: Stays on this machine
local.workspaceFiles: Your workspace files and raw data
local.codeExecution: Code execution — the Python kernel and Jupyter run locally; datasets are processed here, never uploaded in bulk.
local.sessionHistory: Session history and provenance records, in the app's private data folder.
local.providerKeys: Provider keys and login tokens — an app-private file readable only by your account; never written to the workspace, provenance, logs, or exports.

remote.heading: Sent to your model provider
remote.messages: Your messages, and the file contents / command output the agent reads to do the task you asked for.
remote.notBackground: Nothing is sent in the background — data leaves only during a conversation turn.
remote.providerPolicy: What the provider retains is governed by its own data policy.

remote.title: Remote Access
remote.hint: Turn this desktop into a secure API — reach your sessions and files from a phone or another computer on your network, a CLI, or a tunnel. Off by default.
remote.enableHint: Start the authenticated gateway. Bound to this device only until you allow the local network below.
remote.loopbackUrlHint: Open in a browser on this Mac, or point a CLI here.
remote.bindingHint: Where the gateway listens. Only enable the local network on a network you trust.
remote.lanWarn: This exposes the gateway to everyone on your local network. Anyone with the token can drive the agent and read your workspace files. Only do this on a network you trust. Continue?
remote.lanActive: Reachable by other devices on your network. Keep the token secret.
remote.modeFullHint: Clients can create sessions, send prompts, run tools, and answer approvals.
remote.modeReadonlyHint: Clients can read sessions and files only — no prompts, tools, or approvals.
remote.tokenHint: Clients authenticate with this bearer token.
remote.regenerated: New token generated — existing clients must reconnect.
remote.openHint: The copied link includes the token — open it on another device to connect, no typing needed.
remote.connectPrompt: Enter the access token from the desktop app → Settings → Remote Access.
